title: PCCP-Bench v0.1.0 — a judgeable, re-runnable test set for Predetermined Change Control Plan decisions in imaging AI
description:
What this is. A 42-case test set (32 public, 10 committed-but-hidden) plus the reference judge, for the single question a Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP) has to answer per change: go, hold, or reject. Every case carries the regulatory text it rests on, so a third party can disagree on the merits rather than on the plumbing.

What it is not. It is not a regulatory determination, not FDA-endorsed, and not a substitute for a reviewer. Ground truth was rebuilt by us from public FDA guidance and cleared 510(k) summaries; it is our reading, not an agency position.

How to use it. Unzip, then python bench.py --submit your_adapter.py. Your adapter receives one case at a time and returns go/hold/reject with a reason. Scores are exact match, macro recall and a citation-tag score. The reference adapter scores 0.9688 exact on both public and masked columns; the null baseline "always go" scores 0.875 exact but only 0.5 macro recall — a set where the lazy answer wins on the headline number is a set that measures nothing, which is why macro recall is reported beside it.

Reproducibility. The archive is frozen: MANIFEST.json lists the sha256 of all 14 leaves and ROOT.txt carries the Merkle root 2d305387f61808d8d18e2cbb8ff627dc7948a08f37f4b75e6852dc29cdc6de9d (rule: leaf = sha256(path + NUL + file_sha256), pairs hashed together, odd node pairs with itself). Recompute it and you will get the same string, or the archive has been altered.

Known disagreements. 2 of 42 cases (K260973-H1, K260973-N2) are scored hold by our reading and reject by the reference judge. They are published as disagreements rather than silently resolved, because a benchmark that hides its own split judgements is asking to be trusted instead of checked.

Status. Version 0.1.0, 2026-11-26. The hidden 10 cases are committed by hash only and are not in this archive. Anyone is welcome to run it and publish their numbers; disagreement is the point.
notes: Code in this archive (bench.py, build_cases.py, judge_pccp.py) is additionally available under Apache-2.0; the dataset text is CC BY 4.0. Licence split is stated per file in LICENSE_STATUS.md.
